title: Euclid I.Def.3: The ends of a line are points.
summary: Euclid I.Def.3: The ends of a line are points.
body: Euclid, Book I, I.Def.3, as worded on this page: "The ends of a line are points." David E. Joyce's guide on the same page says: "This statement can be taken as indicating that between certain lines and points a relation holds, that a point can be an end of a line. It doesn’t say what ends are. It also doesn’t indicate how many ends a line can have. For instance, the circumference of a circle has no ends, but a finite line has its two end points." Joyce describes his text as similar to Heath's translation of Heiberg, and slightly less literal.
said_by: Euclid, in David E. Joyce's text of the Elements at Clark University
